I've saved the 3Q answers to `answer.json`. I didn't check them against the 2Q reference values, because `CLAUDE.md` says not to compare results with reference values.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | smb, 311,878,960 won |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 246 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | acc, 231,889,770 won |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest refunds | u155@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 694,985 won |
| h. September vs. August growth | 12.8% |

The monthly net sales behind h were 269,431,599 won for August and 304,036,622 won for September.

The data had a few quirks, and I made these calls:
- **Messy segment and category labels:** values like `"Enterprise "`, `" consumer"` and `"SMB"` have stray spaces or capitals. I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate emails:** there are 300 customer IDs but only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f I counted customers by email (trimmed and lowercased). If you count by customer ID instead, b and f may change.
- **Quarter dates:** an order counts if the date part of `ordered_at` (stored in UTC) falls between 2025-07-01 and 2025-09-30.

Because of the duplicate-email choice in particular, it's worth running the same queries on 2Q to confirm they give the reference values.
